mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the cost of capital, increasing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days. The relationship is inverse: as FEDFUNDS decreases, returns increase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is rising (FEDFUNDS change > 0.1% in 3 months) and inflation is high (CPIAUCSL > 300), the market prices in a prolonged tightening cycle, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.1% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL > 300
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS change > 0.1% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL > 300.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a housing market strength (HOUST > 1500) signals overoptimism about economic durability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to anticipated policy tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1500 in late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A higher housing market (HOUST) indicates robust consumer spending, supporting positive equity returns. The relationship is positive: as HOUST increases, S&P 500 returns increase over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when HOUST is above 1400.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) triggers concerns about central bank action, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 300.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS > 155000) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.0%) signals near-full employment, increasing wage pressure and the likelihood of aggressive monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 155000 and UNRATE < 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained environment (INDPRO growth rate < 0.5% in 3 months), the market anticipates reduced economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to lower corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO growth < 0.5% in 3 months.
